values.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

values.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
values.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
values.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.
values.5: Brian Thomas has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last two games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has played fewer than 50% of snaps on offense while being outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers. Thomas is too talented to overlook completely, but he's a risky flex option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London. The matchup would become more favorable if Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) sits. Philadelphia is allowing 162 receiving yards per game to wide receivers.

values.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

values.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
values.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
values.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.
values.5: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

values.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
values.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
values.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
values.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.

values.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
values.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
values.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
values.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.

Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.

Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.
values.4: James Cook figures to see a heavy workload in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Cook has consecutive games with at least 21 carries, topping 134 yards in each while scoring twice. He's not heavily involved in the passing game, with just four catches after at least 32 grabs the last two years, and the return of Ty Johnson doesn't inspire confidence. New England just allowed a season-high 73 yards to Jacksonville's lead back Bhayshul Tuten, but they held Cook to 156 yards in two meetings last year. There's little doubt Cook will be heavily featured, but he may need to reach the end zone for a massive Week 4 contribution.

Cook has now scored in three straight games, but his workload was minimal in Week 4 against New England, rushing a season-low 12 times. The Rams have been stout against the run, not allowing a running back to score through four games and allowing just 3.9 yards per carry, and Cook's lack of involvement in the passing game further dampens the outlook. So long as Buffalo doesn't fall behind early and is forced to throw often, Cook remains stable, but Week 5 profiles as a night to temper lofty expectations.

Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. values.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
values.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
values.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
values.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.

Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Shipley and Tank Bigsby would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge, as the latter had 15 touches and a touchdown to outpace Shipley. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears run defense allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags, as is Barkley's due to a hamstring ailment. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. Shipley did have six rushes for 23 yards following the injury to Bigsby. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.
values.4: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Patriots. Dealing with a Week 3 ankle injury, Coleman caught a 37-yard pass on two targets, a significant decrease in volume with DJ Moore healthy. Moore dominates targets and Buffalo is a run-first offense. Facing a defense that's allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target, there may not be enough opportunities for Coleman to contribute.
values.5: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains unsettled ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. DJ Moore exited Week 4 after aggravating a shoulder injury that forced a similar result in Week 2, and Coleman again shined. In the two games with Moore leaving early, Coleman has 12 catches on 13 targets for 179 yards and a touchdown. With Moore playing four quarters, Coleman has two catches for 38 yards. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards leaves Coleman as a fantasy risk regardless of Moore's status.

Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.

Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
values.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.

The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.

New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.
values.5: DJ Moore continues to battle a shoulder issue as the Bills get set to travel in Week 5 to face the Rams. Moore exited Week 4's game against New England after aggravating the injury, his second early departure in four games. When playing an entire four quarters, Moore has dominated targets from Josh Allen, averaging nine looks. However, pairing injury concerns with the Rams' secondary not allowing an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, Moore could struggle in Week 5.

Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
values.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. values.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. values.5: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
values.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. values.5: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.

If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
values.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
values.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.

His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.

Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.

Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.
values.5: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.

values.5: Kenyon Sadiq faces an unsettled role in the Jets' limited passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. The Browns haven't allowed an opposing tight end to top 51 yards while surrendering just 6.7 yards per target, not boding well for Sadiq in Week 5. values.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. values.5: Spencer Shrader has made all seven of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last two games and all 11 attempts this season. He has been one of the hottest waiver-wire options at kicker over the past couple of weeks and could be worth picking up if he's still available ahead of a Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers have allowed eight made field goals in four games and 21.8 points per game. Those who streamed Shrader against Washington in Week 4 may as well keep rolling with him in Week 5.

values.seasonOutlook: Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

values.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
values.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
values.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
values.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

values.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
values.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
values.4: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
values.5: Malik Nabers exploded last game for 112 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants to victory. Nabers snagged six passes on seven targets for a season-high in terms of receiving yardage. He and quarterback Jameis Winston finally appeared to be on the same page. In Week 5, Nabers and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

values.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.

After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
values.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.
values.5: TreVeyon Henderson will seek chunk plays in the Patriots' Week 5 matchup against a vulnerable Raiders run defense. Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.

values.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

values.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

values.seasonOutlook: Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

Irving could still thrive in Week 5 against a Cowboys defense that's given up 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.

Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.
values.4: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.
values.5: Rhamondre Stevenson continues to share work in the Patriots backfield ahead of an inviting Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and was just solved by Kansas City's Kenneth Walker for 177 yards, so while split work will limit Stevenson's ceiling, his continued involvement as a pass-catcher paired with double-digit carries can result in fantasy-worthy production in Week 5.

values.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

values.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.

values.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.

That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
values.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.
values.5: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.

values.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.

Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.

Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.

Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

values.seasonOutlook: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

Allen had 10 carries in Week 1 under new OC Frank Reich, after totaling 18 carries in four games before injury in 2025. The volume resulted from the Jets playing with a lead, a game script that's unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Allen remains a secondary option to Breece Hall, so patience is warranted, particularly against a defense that allowed only 3.7 yards per carry in Week 1 and is more vulnerable through the air.

He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.
values.4: Braelon Allen is poised for an expanded role in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears due to Breece Hall's thigh injury. The rushing game has struggled over the last two weeks, averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry, but the Jets have remained committed to running while also involving their backs in the passing game. With volume seemingly secure, Allen could shine against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry.
values.5: Braelon Allen could be slated for bulk carries in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns with Breece Hall's (quad) uncertain availability. Filling in for Hall in Week 4, Allen was the only Jet to receive a carry, putting him in line to potentially exploit a Cleveland defense that's allowed at least 82 yards to opposing lead backs in three straight weeks and an appealing 4.8 yards per carry. If Hall returns, he can't be guaranteed a full workload, lending flex appeal to Allen.

values.seasonOutlook: A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are established as lead backs, so there's an opportunity for Allen to force his way into a larger role. The 22-year-old is worth no more than a late-round flier.

The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.

Love carried the ball 21 times against San Francisco this past Sunday, while Allgeier handled a season-low two totes. The latter did reel in a season-best four catches, but they amounted to just 10 receiving yards. Though the Giants are struggling against the run, ranking in the bottom half of the league in allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game to RBs, Allgeier will likely need to see more opportunities in order to make an impact.

Even with Love healthy for nearly the entire game in Week 4, Allgeier posted good production, recording an 8-42-1 rushing line and two catches for seven yards. The Cardinals' RB group could find success against a Lions defense that is giving up 4.64 yards per carry to running backs, eighth-worst in the league.

values.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.

Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.

Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.
values.5: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He corralled five of six targets for 27 yards and his first touchdown of the season in Baltimore's Week 4 win. Andrews has yet to top 50 yards receiving through four outings to date, and that trend could continue if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to play on Sunday Night Football. The veteran tight end will aim to find paydirt for the second straight week against Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (15.9) per game to the position.

He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try.
